claim_detail.motion_result: no motion plan found for the final descent to inverted_u_yellow_placement after repeated attempts (including solve_ik_first, which timed out)

payload.notes: Between completing place_approach_inverted_u_yellow and attempting the final descent, u_brown, u_orange and line_green -- all previously verified within tolerance -- were found displaced far beyond their disturbance tolerances; u_orange in particular is now off the fixture entirely. The registry's acm_allowed_object_pairs (needed for planning tractability around intended contacts) covers every pair including inverted_u_yellow against the three seated parts, so MoveIt's planner did not flag contact between the held part/arm and those seated parts as a collision while transporting and staging inverted_u_yellow in this tightly packed region -- but the task's own working notes are explicit that this ACM setting carries no permission for that contact to actually happen, and the invariant against disturbing seated parts was violated here even though no planner error was raised. The final descent itself also then failed to find a motion plan (and solve_ik_first timed out), consistent with the fixture-area geometry no longer being clear. I retreated the arm (lift + safe pose) and am holding the run rather than attempting further motion in this contaminated region.

payload.reason: u_brown, u_orange and line_green -- all previously seated within tolerance -- were found displaced far beyond their disturbance tolerances while transporting/staging inverted_u_yellow (u_orange knocked entirely off the fixture); the final descent for inverted_u_yellow then failed to find a motion plan. Retreated the arm to the safe pose rather than risk further contact in the contaminated region; assembly is not complete.

detail.root_cause_hypothesis: acm_allowed_object_pairs covers every pair among the five parts for planner tractability; this suppressed MoveIt's collision checking between the held inverted_u_yellow (and arm) and the three already-seated parts in a tightly-packed fixture region, so the planner did not flag the contact that disturbed them even though the task's invariants prohibit disturbing seated parts
